text:
San Jose and Nashville both open the night having been outchanced more often than not, but the gap between them is real. At five on five, SJS has taken 39% of the expected goals this season and NSH 41%. The Sharks allow 3.79 expected goals per 60 against 3.00 for the Predators, and they've given up 3.83 goals a game to Nashville's 3.00. The model projects NSH 3.31 to SJS 3.0 tonight. On special teams, Nashville's penalty kill allows 0.61 expected goals a game, well under San Jose's 1.05, while the power plays are close (0.62 for NSH, 0.59 for SJS).

The projected goalies are Yaroslav Askarov for SJS and Juuse Saros for NSH, and neither has been sharp. Askarov is at .848 and -1.4 goals saved above expected this season after -19.4 over 47 games last year. Saros is at .897 and -0.38 this season, after -10.19 over 59 games last year. Askarov has the thinner track record, and with the Sharks giving up so many quality chances, that could matter.

Form favors Nashville too. NSH is 2-1-2 in its last five with 48% of the expected goals, and the 2-5 loss to VGK on Oct. 13 came in a game it outchanced, 53%. SJS is 2-3-0 with 35% of the expected goals and hasn't won a chance battle in any of those games. Among the players the model likes, Macklin Celebrini has a 38% chance to score and the same figure for two or more points. For Nashville, Steven Stamkos is at 41% to score and Filip Forsberg at 38%.
